newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank buys dollars at 26.362 pesos.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank buys dollars at 26.362 pesos.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank bought dollars in the midsession on Friday, switching from its earlier selling of the U.S. currency, traders said.
The Central Bank purchased about $20 to $40 million at 26.362 pesos for delivery today, traders said.
Banks have been nervous about possible capital flight after heavy foreign sales of local shares.
Traders said banks started selling their dollars after the Central Bank showed its determination to limit the peso's fall.
"Moreover, the pressure to hold dollars was not so much," a foreign bank dealer said, since the Central Bank offered five-day reverse repos at 11.0 percent.
Late Wednesday, the Central Bank had decided to raise its overnight borrowing rate to 11.0 percent from 10.25 percent to pre-empt peso speculation.
Earlier in the day, the Central Bank sold dollars to meet actual demand for the currency from foreign investors, traders said.
Banks had also tested the Central Bank's resolve to keep the peso at 26.375, which later led banks to unload their dollars, traders said.
